_what: EVERY constant of the g-xTB v1.1 method that does NOT live in the official parameter files (gxtb_parameters / basisq / eeq) -- decoded from reference sources or MEASURED from the oracle, one table each, loaded once at start (constants.py). Nothing in the prototype may hardcode a method constant; this file is the single home. Provenance per entry.
_rule: If a value here disagrees with a new measurement, the MEASUREMENT wins and this file gets the update + a provenance note. Values marked 'measured' carry the experiment that produced them.

onsite_electronic_measured._note: charted from the oracle (chart_onsite.py + ion-channel scans); closed forms partly identified. All PROVEN hardcoded in the binary.
onsite_electronic_measured.equal_U_decomposition: ES23(ion; U=u,u) = A + B*u + C*u^2 fits EXACTLY (3-point); B = (s/2)*q_A^2 (even, quadratic to 5 digits); C = k3*q_A^3*u^2-coefficient (cubic to 4 digits); A = u-independent remainder entangled with ion shell redistribution

s_rule._form: s = a_p * Nval + b_p  (linear in valence-electron count WITHIN a period; 9 elements, max dev 2e-4)
s_rule._caveat: d-block/heavy ions (Ge test) show shell-redistribution contamination -- extraction needs population tracking there

third_order_u2_rule._form: the u^2 coefficient = k3 * q_A^3 (exact for C and O across +-1, +-2)
third_order_u2_rule._caveat: row-2 C..O linear (+0.0073/Z) but F breaks it -- F/heavier extractions need the per-state check; refine next

third_order_shape._form: E3_onsite = c1_el * q_A * sum_ll' q_l q_l' (U_l+U_l')^2/4  (the Eq.132 DEGREE-2 kernel applied onsite -- NOT the harmonic the garbled SI line suggested; explains the u^2 rule)
third_order_shape._evidence: chart_onsite2.py: per-point populations + s-rule subtracted; c1 consistent across +- states (F: 0.01628/0.01627; C-1 captures 99.4% of a 0.17 Eh signal at 1e-3)
third_order_shape._resolved: v1's 'F k3 anomaly' dissolved -- F was right; the row-2 linear k3 trend was the artifact of the wrong (u^2-only) shape
third_order_shape._open: C+1 and O+2 carry unmodeled structure (shell-resolved quartic candidate); c1's element rule not yet identified; d-block extraction needs population tracking

slot_assignments_molecular._source: FD response-shape probing on the HCl stretch at R=2/3/5 bohr (thirteenth-fourteenth pushes)
slot_assignments_molecular.L1[7]: Hamiltonian-basis scale (moves charges; response persists at dissociation)
slot_assignments_molecular.L1[8]: k1CN -- chemical-potential CN-dependence (SI Eq. 84); H 0.775 magnitude-verified
slot_assignments_molecular.G2[1]: offsite ES kernel global (k2x candidate; ES23 response ~constant R=3..5)
slot_assignments_molecular._rejected: a 5-parameter forward fit converged at k1CN~-23 (100x the SI scale) -- rejected as wrong-structure per house rules; slot identification by response SHAPES instead, magnitudes to be verified by forward model with FILE values
slot_assignments_molecular._eq85_resolved: VISUAL read of SI p.47-48 (rendered PNG): Eq.85 as PRINTED carries a subscript typo (l_B left, l_A right); intent per prose: drho_l = aufbau_l - refocc_l, static and per-shell small (near-cancelling atom sums). The fast-decaying stretch signal was the k1CN onsite term (L1[8]); the true offsite E1 is tiny. First-order term fully accounted for: mu=L7, k1CN=L1[8], f-switching globals hardcoded.
slot_assignments_molecular.mu_cn_structure: MEASURED (machine-precision FD via restart-density charges, HCl R=2..4): the mu CN-coupling is SQRT(CN)-structured -- direct/(mu*q) tracks sqrt(CN_mean) at ratio 1.07-1.21 across the range while every other candidate varies by factors. Same family as repulsion Eq. 56; the SI's Eq. 84 prints plain CN_A -- another paper-vs-binary divergence (pattern: Eq. 55 factor 2, Eq. 84 sqrt). OPEN: amplitude ~1.49x the file k1 value and a smooth 6% shape drift -- rc/amplitude separable by multi-partner stretches (HF/HBr), designed next.

mu_cn_multipartner._data: x = dES1/dk1H/(mu_H*q_H) vs R for HF/HCl/HBr (restart-precision charges)
mu_cn_multipartner.implied_per_pair: solving x = k_eff*sqrt(CN(R; rc)) per pair: rc(HF)~0.99, rc(HCl)~1.465, rc(HBr)~1.82 with k_eff F~1.22, Cl~1.29, Br~1.50 (Br's constant to 0.3% over its scan)
mu_cn_multipartner._verdict: sqrt(CN)-family CONFIRMED per-pair, but the effective radii match NO decoded set (element diffs 0.475/0.355 vs L1[5] 0.783/0.508, Pyykko 0.662/0.283) and k_eff is partner-dependent -- either mu-CN has its own radius table (hardcoded) or a second CN-like term overlaps. Next discriminator: dense R-scans per pair for exact (k_eff, rc) + joint solve across many partners for a per-element radius table.

mu_cn_own_table._conclusion: the mu-CN uses its OWN hardcoded per-element geometry (the FOURTH hardcoded table): dense scans exclude every decoded radius set (L1[5], Pyykko, CEH, EEQBC-cov, vdW, Slater) under free-(keff,rc) fits, AND per-pair steepness varies (-2.39..-1.44) under fixed-radii fits -- no shared convention reproduces all pairs
mu_cn_own_table.fit_quality: sqrt(CN) shape explains 99%+ per pair (worst resid 9e-4 for HBr)
mu_cn_own_table._closure_design: triangulation: perturb the PARTNER's k1CN in mixed X-Y pairs -> rc(X,Y) directly; enough pairs over-determine the per-element radius table (up to the combination convention); relaxation subtraction via restart-density charges throughout

mu_cn_pair_function._finding: BOTH atoms of a pair share the same C(R): Cl-side on HCl fits (keff 1.2484, rc 1.4742) vs H-side (1.2929, 1.4708) -- the mu-CN count is a PAIR property (the same bond counted from both ends), so per-element radii combine to the measured pair rc
mu_cn_pair_function.es1_closure_hcl: forward model with measured pair C(R) (keff 1.2707, rc 1.4725 avg) + static drho offsite + KO kernel: worst |d| 2.4e-3 at R=2 (was 1.0e-2), mid/long range 1e-4..4e-4
mu_cn_pair_function._remaining: R=2 residual suspects: relaxation contamination in keff (~5%), f-linearization at |q|~0.33, offsite k2x screening
